questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Somewhere that was different from my home country but still not too far away. And that it was possbible to take some interesting courses that was relevant for me.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had a lot of bad luck in the beginning of the semester: two of my courses were in Portuguese and I had to move apartment because of a terrible experience with my landlord and the place I was renting. But after I had solved these issues, everything was very much what I had hoped. I met a lot of interesting people from other countries and from my own university as well, and I enjoyed being challenges at school with new courses and ways of learning, even though it could be challenging at times. But the challenges only made me value my home institution more, and gave me a new perspective on what I am used to having at home.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Not very easy. The university was really old school and not easy to navigate in in terms of documentation and courses. I needed more practical information, and found it very difficult to get the help that I needed, but I think it was because I was very unlucky in the beginning, because I had to change two of my courses while I also had to keep up with the other three courses at the same time.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I asked the international office for help, the First Lady (the director) was not very helpful, but then another lady (Ana?) helped me a lot after I asked for help the third time. She really helped me a lot.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I think I was left alone to deal with the problems with my courses, and I really needed some guidance as I am not used to their kind of system: I had to print a document (where?) and run around to find the different teachers (that I had no idea how looked) in different classrooms (that I had no idea where was) to get their signature (if they approved of me attending their course). This was a super stressfull way to start my semester. I think it would have been great if someone had told me exactly how to do this, instead of me spending a whole week trying to figure it out, and going back ond forth to the international office.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Not easy. Try to ask earlier exchange students for recommendations, as that is probably the only way to be 100% sure that the landlord is trustable. If the price is low and does not match the location or size, it is probably too good to be true. I would really recommend searching in areas outside of the center, as this is where you can find really good places for a fair price. The metro works really well, so it is much better to live 10 minutes away from the center, instead of living in the chaos with noise and probably a way too high rent. I lived in Anjos and I really liked the area.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I enjoyed living near the city, and not at campus. I could walk (1 hour) to school or take the metro (20 minutes), so it was no problem living off campus for me.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I could have used more advice or guidance in where to look for housing, but I understand that it is not very easy to guide students when they want to live off campus.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Not easy as mentioned above.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Really really bad. the courses was apparently not in English as promised, so I had to change courses and it was such an awful expererience where I had to get a document and run around for signatures from teachers who I did not know and in a campus I had no chance to navigate in

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The international office

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I had problems changing courses upon arrival. It was really hard to understand the procedure.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Go to the international office and ask for them to print the document for changing courses. Ask them very directly to help you find new courses and where to find the teachers etc.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Some classes were really interesting (visual culture, American history, language and communication, contemporary drama). but the course that I thought I would enjoy the most, was really bad (Study of cultures). The teacher is really crazy and yells at the students and says really problematic things to the students. I hope he we get fired as all the students hated to be in his classes because of his way of talking (and his way of teaching).

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think the level was perfect in terms on learning new things but also not getting overwhelmed by too high levels. So, I learned interesting new things but did not have to fight to keep up with the topics or homework.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Not as good as my home institution: Lisbon was more oldschool with no good powerpoints, no clear information, no clear structure in most of the classes, bad climatic environment in the classrooms without breaks or group work to change the energy. But I learned how to deal with it and managed to get used to how they did it.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Contemporary drama, Visual culture, Study of cultures, language and communication, History of the US (colonial to 1900)

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Visual culture ! Very interesting and I likes the teacher Paula a lot. Also, History of the US (colonial to 1900) was interesting. And Contemporary Drama was nice because it was different from what I am used to, and the teacher had a very good energy and not as conservative as the other teachers.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had to move, and did not get my deposit back.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Eating out is cheap, Alcohol is cheap. uber is very cheap and I would recommend using It in the evenings especially.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not use it.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sports and clubs

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Surf school. Hiking trails (there are a lot in 1-hour distance from Lisbon). Roadtrip down south or to Eirica - a lot of nice beaches and cute small cities. Also go and watch a football game, It is a big experience watching Portugal play.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Nazare, erica, sintra (for hiking. take the train in the morning and hike up to the castles). Go to the beach or chill in all the cute parks in Lisbon.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy as the culture is not that different from Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be open and ask questions. Also, try to do something active with them as hiking or surfing.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The language barrier, not all Portuguese people speak English, so try to learn a few Portuguese words to make it easier to communicate. But I would say that most people are good at speaking English.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food (fresh fish and the culture around eating out and going out also in weekdays) and the amazing nature! Also, I appreciated how the people are very direct and not shy or introvert as Danes might be to strangers.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Don't take the course Study of culture, as the teacher is very bad and not nice. 
2. Come to the intro-day as it helps a lot to meet the other students and get to see the school before your first day. 
3. You can buy food and coffee in the cantina or in the cafe, and there is student cafe where you can sit and work.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is very old school in terms of technology and classroom communication, so bring cold water for the warm days and make sure that you have power on your devices when going to class.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To meet a lot of new friends, experiencing the beautiful nature and eating amazing food everyday.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: That I had to move apartment after two weeks because of the bad housing. But it was worth it, and I ended up living with two other danish girls in a very nice apartment in Anjos.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
